harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: inventory-api is running persistently on node1 and remained healthy during a confirmed global OOM event while the kernel killed the designated memory hog. It also recovered automatically after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated inventory-api system account and JSON HTTP service on port 8080.
Installed and enabled a hardened systemd unit with Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-900, ManagedOOMPreference=avoid, and MemoryMin=64M.
Generated controlled global memory pressure with a transient hog configured at OOMScoreAdjust=1000.
Confirmed the kernel OOM killer stopped the hog while inventory-api retained the same PID and continued serving HTTP 200.
Safely restarted node1 and verified a changed boot identity and complete service recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as an enabled, managed service with OOM protection
evidence.summary: The systemd unit was validated, enabled, active, listening on port 8080, and serving /health and /inventory with live OOM score -900.

evidence.requirement: The memory hog is killed by the kernel while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: Before pressure, inventory-api was healthy as PID 1657. Kernel logs then recorded constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE, global_oom and killed hog PID 1729 with oom_score_adj=1000. inventory-api remained active on PID 1657 and returned a healthy response afterward.

Pre-restart boot ID was 5f3ce3b8-4860-447e-bcf1-d6643718694e with a healthy API. The reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to b1102da2-f16f-4725-b32e-d9c157687796, and node1 returned to running state with inventory-api enabled, active, score -900, listening, and serving both endpoints.
